W08.title: Schedule a ride for later, then cancel
W08.shows: Rider switches Private to "Later", picks a pickup time, books; the ride waits as "Scheduled"; when the wake fires the server starts searching ("Finding your driver"); the rider reopens the page and sees the searching state; the rider cancels.
W08.transitions: requested (type=scheduled, wake job delayed to T-10 min) -> [wake job runs] dispatch starts, still requested -> cancelled (cancelled_by=client, wake job removed).
W08.notes: The wake job normally fires scheduled.wakeLeadMs (10 min) before pickup, and the earliest bookable pickup is 15 min out, so a real wake is >= 5 min after booking. The harness promotes the delayed BullMQ job (lib/devstack.ts promoteScheduledWake) so the real wake worker runs immediately. No driver is online in this area, so the search has no taker; the "Still looking ... until <time>" copy comes from the ride:snapshot (retryUntil = pickup + scheduled.retryCutoffAfterPickupMs); the live ride_dispatch_retry push (first re-arm) arrives only after the 4-minute scheduled accept window (scheduled.dispatchWindowMs) and is not part of this recording.

W01.title: Landing page and route guard
W01.shows: The public landing page, its two entry points, and the booking page bouncing an anonymous visitor to sign-in.
W01.transitions: No ride states. Anonymous visitor: / -> /book -> redirected to /signin (withAuth route guard).

W02.title: Sign-in screen (phone OTP UI)
W02.shows: The phone-number step of sign-in, client-side validation, and the form layout. No OTP is sent.
W02.transitions: No ride states. Sign-in is Firebase phone OTP -> POST /v1/auth/firebase-exchange -> access token + refresh cookie (not exercised here).
W02.notes: UI only by design: the OTP step needs a real SMS. The flows that sit behind sign-in (W03-W10) start from a harness-created session instead (README, "Sessions").

W03.title: Normal ride: quote to rating
W03.shows: Passenger quotes and books a private ride; a driver accepts and drives it to completion; passenger rates the driver.
W03.transitions: requested -> dispatching -> accepted -> en_route -> arrived -> in_progress -> completed, then rating

W05.title: Driver cancels, then reports a no-show
W05.shows: Two rides back to back. Ride 1: the driver cancels while en route. Ride 2: the driver arrives, waits out the no-show window and reports the rider as a no-show.
W05.transitions: Ride 1: requested -> accepted -> en_route -> cancelled (cancelled_by=driver, reason required). Ride 2: requested -> accepted -> en_route -> arrived -> no_show.
W05.notes: The no-show is only allowed 5 minutes after `arrived` (policy rides.noShowWaitMs). The harness back-dates rides.arrived_at by 6 minutes in the DEV database instead of recording a 5-minute wait (apps/web/e2e/demo/lib/fixtures.ts backdateArrival). Everything else goes through the real API. The simulated driver stands in for the Flutter app; the driver-app videos (D07) show the real driver UI for the same actions.

W10.title: Sign out revokes the session
W10.shows: A signed-in rider signs out; the app returns to /signin and a reload of /book can no longer silently log back in.
W10.transitions: No ride states. POST /v1/auth/logout revokes the refresh token and clears the cookie; /book then redirects to /signin.

W04.title: Passenger cancels before pickup
W04.shows: Rider books, a driver accepts and starts driving, then the rider cancels from the tracking panel.
W04.transitions: requested -> dispatching -> accepted -> en_route -> cancelled (cancelled_by=client). No fee in Phase-0.
W04.notes: The Cancel button is only offered before in_progress; the API rejects a client cancel once the trip started (rides.clientCancellableFrom in docs/POLICY.md).

W09.title: Reload and reconnect restore tracking
W09.shows: Mid-ride the rider reloads the page, then loses the realtime connection while the driver arrives; both times the tracking view recovers the true state.
W09.transitions: Reload: session from refresh cookie + ride from GET /v1/rides/:id + ride:snapshot. Drop: WebSocket blocked while the driver goes en_route -> arrived; on reconnect the ride:snapshot catches the UI up.
W09.notes: The connection loss is simulated with Playwright page.routeWebSocket (closes every socket.io connection), then removed so socket.io-client reconnects by itself.

W06.title: No driver available
W06.shows: Rider books while no driver is online nearby; dispatch widens wave 1 to wave 2, then hard-fails after 60 s.
W06.transitions: requested -> dispatching (wave 1: 2 km, wave 2 at +30 s: 4 km) -> no_driver at +60 s (dispatch.waveOneTimeoutMs / hardFailMs).
W06.notes: Recorded at the shipped default windows (no env overrides, api not restarted): the 60 s wait is real time.

W07.title: Shared ride: two passengers, one cab
W07.shows: Two riders on similar routes book a share; the second joins the first rider's pool, the pool closes when its 60 s window ends, a driver claims it and works the pickup/drop-off itinerary to completion. Left panel = rider 1, right panel = rider 2.
W07.transitions: Pool: open (seat 1) -> open (seat 2 joined; max_seats is 3) -> closed_timeout (60 s after opening) -> driver offer accepted (claimed) -> closed_started (first pickup confirmed) -> completed (last drop-off confirmed).
W07.notes: Side by side: two recorded browser contexts (640x720 each) composed with ffmpeg hstack, aligned to the moment the second context opened. The pool window (matching.poolTimeoutMs, 60 s) is real time, no env overrides. With the shipped matching.maxSeats = 3 two riders do not fill the pool, so it closes by timeout (closed_timeout); a third rider joining inside the window would close it as closed_full instead (state-machines.md, section 3). The rider UI shows pool status and seat count but no map tracking for shared rides (a product gap, listed in the web INDEX). The driver is the simulator (lib/driver-sim.ts) confirming stops over the real Socket.IO events.
